question: Does the 2026 Luzon paper support a source-attributed Decapterus smithvanizi record in Cagayan, and how precisely can its market specimens be assigned to a capture locality?

method.summary: Retrieved and visually reviewed all seven pages of the J-STAGE publisher PDF. Checked the abstract, materials and methods, figure captions, specimen material examined, meristic and morphometric tables, identification discussion, distribution, acknowledgements, publisher article metadata and license statement. No machine-readable dataset, coordinates, accession sequence, or separate supplement was identified in the reviewed publisher record.
method.publisherPage: J-STAGE identifies the peer-reviewed open-access article as Biogeography volume 29 (2026), DOI 10.11358/biogeo.29.35, published 2026-05-27, and states CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.
method.retrieval: Full article PDF downloaded from the J-STAGE publisher link for review; it was not copied into the repository.

study.citation: Hata, H., Maeda, K., Sallan, L., de Peralta-Banauag, G., Ziegler, J. T., & Ballad, E. L. (2026). First records of Decapterus smithvanizi (Teleostei: Carangidae) from Luzon, Philippines. Biogeography, 29, 35–40. https://doi.org/10.11358/biogeo.29.35.
study.bibliographicPageRangeNote: J-STAGE metadata and the article's first-page header give pages 35–40, while the final page of the retrieved PDF is numbered 41. The citation follows the publisher's page-range metadata pending clarification.
study.fieldContext: Joint OIST, Cagayan State University, and BFAR Region II work; acknowledgements state the survey operated under an agreement among CSU, BFAR Region II and OIST and cite Gratuitous Permit No. 0381-26 and Export Commodity Clearance ECC0026-002.
study.samplingDesign: Three fish specimens acquired from the fishery supply chain and morphologically examined; collection localities were investigated through interviews with staff at a retailer in Don Domingo Public Market. This is not a standardized ecological abundance survey.

sourceReportedTaxon.identificationBasis: The authors describe diagnostic morphology and compare the specimens with published descriptions. The article identifies the specimens as D. smithvanizi and illustrates them with specimen catalogue numbers.
sourceReportedTaxon.internalDiagnosticConflict: The identification text gives 54–57 cycloid scales on the curved lateral line for the Luzon specimens, while Table 1 lists 55, 57, and 52 for OISTICH 2467, 2468, and 2469 respectively. Preserve the discrepancy; do not silently correct the value or independently resolve the third specimen's identification from this review.

localityAndDate.sourceReportedCaptureOrigin: Off Santa Ana, Province of Cagayan, Luzon, Philippines.
localityAndDate.originEvidence: The abstract says the fish were caught near Santa Ana; the methods state that localities were investigated by interviews with staff at a fish retailer in Don Domingo Public Market. The material-examined line associates the specimens with off Santa Ana and records their purchase at the Tuguegarao market.
localityAndDate.marketVenue: Don Domingo Public Market, Tuguegarao City, Cagayan.
localityAndDate.spatialLimit: The paper's map marks Santa Ana at regional scale. It supplies no coordinates, named fishing ground, gear, vessel track, capture-event identifier, or interview transcript. The market location is not the capture location. Do not infer a municipal-water polygon, a specific reef, river mouth, or point geometry.

photoAssessment.sourceFigure: Figure 1 identifies fresh Decapterus smithvanizi specimens OISTICH 2467–2469; the figure caption and material-examined section link the depicted fish to the named vouchers.
photoAssessment.imageToTaxonEvidence: Direct source attribution with specimen catalogue numbers; the same taxonomic diagnostic-count conflict remains relevant to specimen 2469.
photoAssessment.reuse: The publisher states CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 for the article. No figure was copied or added to Bangwit's species image catalog; image-specific and product-use compatibility have not been approved.

interpretation: The paper is direct, voucher-backed evidence that the authors identified three specimens as D. smithvanizi and attributed their capture to off Santa Ana, Cagayan using retailer interviews.
The specimens were acquired at a Tuguegarao City market on 29 January 2026; this is not the capture date or a Tuguegarao-water occurrence.

The Santa Ana capture origin is a source-reported interview attribution without coordinates or a named fishing ground. Keep it at the source's locality precision and separate it from any site geometry.
The authors call these the first Luzon records. This review records that as the paper's claim and does not treat it as proof of absence in other Luzon locations.
The discussion's market-abundance and schooling statements are not quantified survey results; do not turn them into abundance, seasonality, behavior, or catchability guidance.
The paper's own scale-count narrative conflicts with Table 1 for specimen OISTICH 2469. Retain the source identification and the unresolved conflict together; do not silently normalize the count.

The paper's CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 terms and unverified product-use compatibility do not authorize a Bangwit image or data projection in this review. No occurrence row, canonical species assertion, coordinates, geometry, photo, diet, legal, safety, or public-app data is added.
J-STAGE metadata and the first-page header cite pages 35–40, but the final page of the retrieved PDF is numbered 41; the source citation follows publisher metadata pending clarification.

decision.reason: A full-text peer-reviewed paper reports three examined vouchers with an interview-attributed Santa Ana capture origin, but provides no georeferenced fishing event, has an internal diagnostic-count discrepancy, and carries CC BY-NC-ND terms. Preserve it as bounded research evidence only.

nextAction: Keep the Cagayan record at province/locality level in research review. If the source authors or OISTICH collection provide a specimen-to-capture-event dataset, obtain its locality, capture date, gear, retailer interview method and any coordinates under documented permission; recheck the scale-count discrepancy from the voucher before considering a canonical species row. Review the article's photo separately under the image-source policy before any use.
